local_state_rules: Instructions advance through IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB stages one cycle at a time.
RAW dependencies require forwarding or stalls before the dependent EX stage.
A taken branch flushes younger wrong-path instructions unless prediction already matched.
difficulty_profile: cycle grid, hazard labels, CPI, and controls must share one pipeline state
branch/cache modes add consequences without replacing previous hazard logic
primary visual must be domain-native simulated object, not a pure chart/table/line diagram
task_world.visual_object_requirement: The UI must include a processor pipeline simulation with visible stage boxes/registers, instruction tokens moving through hardware-like lanes, stalls/flush bubbles, and hazard wires/arrows; a table alone is not sufficient.

validation_scenarios.name: pipeline explanation and cycle grid
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T1 asks for explanation and interactive five-stage pipeline UI.
validation_scenarios.oracle: Assistant text explains stages and hazards; UI shows a cycle-by-cycle grid whose stepping advances instructions through stages. The primary visual is a domain-native simulated object rather than only curves, tables, cards, or abstract line art. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.
validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Only require a simple instruction list in turn 1. Do not let actor/evaluator substitute an easier example after a public or UI-advertised boundary case fails; count stale linked views, dummy controls, and impossible success states as real failures. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.

evidence_requirements.expect: explains IF/ID/EX/MEM/WB and why hazards matter

evidence_requirements.surface: visible controls / primary visual / derived readouts
evidence_requirements.expect: At least two independent surfaces change consistently from the same canonical state; a static diagram plus unrelated readout is insufficient.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the most central state-changing control for this turn. First record the visible baseline value on the control plus at least two dependent surfaces, then change the control through a visible UI action. If a range click does not change the value, try direct text input on that same range/text control before giving up. Do not use source code alone as evidence.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the exact before and after control value plus two dependent visible outputs such as readout value, plotted marker, warning text, selected item, table row, or diagram label. If only the control label changes while dependent surfaces do not, report partial or failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must either update according to the domain rule or explicitly explain why the state is impossible; stale values, impossible success states, or generic success text count as failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Exercise one high/low, valid/invalid, legal/blocked, narrow/wide, or correct/wrong contrast that is directly implied by the public request. Prefer a contrast with a predicted qualitative outcome, not a cosmetic setting.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the attempted contrast, the expected domain outcome, and the observed UI outcome. Do not replace a failed public or UI-advertised contrast with an easier passing example when deciding success.

evidence_requirements.expect: All linked surfaces must agree on the same selected entity/time/range/threshold; a view that still shows stale out-of-range data is failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the primary selection, filter, threshold, brush, or range control and inspect every linked surface named by the public request. If direct dragging fails, try visible numeric range inputs, preset buttons, keyboard focus plus arrow keys, or direct input on the same control when available; if no visible path works, report the primary interaction as unreachable rather than substituting an unrelated card click.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the selected value/range and at least three linked surfaces when present. Name any surface that remains out of sync, unchanged, or unreachable.

evidence_requirements.expect: Traces, gauges, warnings, and explanation must change coherently with the same model; static thresholds detached from the simulation are failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Push the model into two qualitatively different regimes using visible controls, such as low/high, safe/unsafe, stable/unstable, before/after disturbance, or valid/invalid. Inspect readouts, traces, warnings, and explanatory labels together.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record both regimes and the corresponding before/after values or warning text. If traces, gauges, warnings, and explanation disagree, report failure.

turns.prompt: Explain how a five-stage CPU pipeline works, then build an interactive cycle grid where I can step instructions through IF, ID, EX, MEM, and WB. Please make the pipeline look like moving instructions through hardware stages, not only a spreadsheet.
Add RAW hazard detection. Let me toggle forwarding versus stalling and show how the pipeline timing changes.
Add a branch instruction with prediction. If the branch is mispredicted, show which younger instructions get flushed.
Add a memory-load cache miss penalty. A miss should hold the MEM stage and affect dependent instructions instead of just adding a note.
Make a practice mode where I reorder a short instruction sequence and compare the old and new CPI with the hazards explained.
